text:
B: Hiya! Oh, hello. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yeah, fine. I'm Kerry.
B: Claire. I'm in Otley, near Leeds. Are you up north as well? I'm guessing from the voice.
A: Washington, near Sunderland.
B: Oh, lovely. I had a friend at uni from Sunderland, she used to call everyone "pet" and I was so jealous. What do you do?
A: Team leader at a contact centre. Broadband and TV complaints, mostly. I've got fourteen on my team.
B: Fourteen! That's a lot of people to keep an eye on.
A: It's fine. Most of them are good. You get the odd one who's always got an excuse.
B: Ha, I bet you sort them out. I'm a speech and language therapist, NHS, with little kids. Three days a week.
A: Three days? That must be nice.
B: It is, honestly. I went part-time when my son was small and just never went back up. I like having days for other stuff, you know, my choir, my printing, walking the dog. I'm very lucky, I know that.
A: I'm doing fifty-odd hours most weeks with overtime. I'd love to cut back but the overtime pays for Tenerife.
B: Oh, do you go every year?
A: Every year. All-inclusive, same sort of hotel. You know where you are with it.
B: I can see the appeal, honestly. I'm terrible, I book everything last minute and I nearly missed a flight to Krakow once. Mark was not impressed. We do a lot of city breaks, wandering round eating things.
A: Krakow. Never fancied it, to be honest. I like a pool and a sunbed.
B: Ha, fair enough, love. Is that a dog bed in your photo?
A: Tia. Staffy. She's eating the settee cushions one at a time.
B: Oh no! Mine's Biscuit, a lurcher, and it's socks with him. He takes them in the garden. Gemma's got a lurcher too, did you talk to Gemma?
A: Yeah, she was sound. Her partner's called Dean, same as mine.
B: No! That's brilliant. Erm, so what do you do when you're not working fifty hours, then?
A: Walk the dog. Watch telly. Sunday tea at my mam's. Bingo with her sometimes.
B: Oh, that's nice. My mum was a dinner lady, and we'd go to bingo at the club. Are you close with her?
A: Yeah. My mam was a dinner lady as well, actually.
B: Really? See, we're all dinner ladies' kids in this study, I think. Is your dad still around?
A: He is. Had a heart scare last year, so we keep an eye on him. He's alright now.
B: Oh, that's a worry, isn't it. My dad's got early dementia, so I'm back and forth to Wakefield helping Mum. Sorry, that's a bit heavy for three minutes.
A: Nah, you're alright. It's hard, that. Does your mum cope?
B: Mostly. She's tougher than me. Anyway! Do you do anything arty? I've got ink all over my hands from lino printing.
A: Not really. I've never even been to the Baltic and it's half an hour away.
B: Oh, you should go, it's free, and there's a—
A: I know, everyone says.
